analyst_view.overall: Brighton played away at Getafe in the Conference League on Thursday, so Fabian Hurzeler may rotate. Mitoma, Tzimas, Azeez and Ferguson are listed as out, and Kadioglu and Struijk are doubts. Keith Andrews' Brentford have had a full week's rest since beating Nottingham Forest, report no new injuries, and have Yarmoliuk back from suspension.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Brighton have conceded only twice in their last six games, and a Thursday trip to Spain plus missing attackers (Mitoma, Ferguson, Tzimas) could take some edge off them. That points to a slightly tighter game than the model expects.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners. Brighton should still have most of the ball against a Brentford side that is happy to counter quickly, so the usual pattern holds.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. Michael Oliver is in charge; he sent off Mateta at Tottenham last week, but we found nothing about this matchup that clearly moves the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with 19.1 of them Brighton's, which is a lot to expect from a side that played in Europe three days earlier and may make changes. A well-rested Brentford are likely to sit compact and break, so we lean a little lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Brentford have scored in every league game and are dangerous on the break through Schade and Ouattara, which offsets a possibly rotated Brighton attack.
